story.title: Sāvitrī river curse, goddess śamī tapas and restored gods with river aṃśas

event.details: At Mahābala, the hurried sacrifice neglects Gaṇeśa and Sāvitrī and seats Gāyatrī. Sāvitrī’s curse becomes river forms at the petitioners’ request, including Śiva/Veṇyā and Kṛṣṇa/Kṛṣṇā.

evidence.paraphrase: Gṛtsamada describes Śiva, Girijā, gaṇas and sages at Mahābala in Sahyādri. Brahmā comes with two wives for a sacrifice; Śiva summons Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha, Mārkaṇḍeya, Nārada, Kapila, Pulaha, Kaṇva, Viśvāmitra, Trita, Dvita and others. Hurrying at the chosen morning time, they forget Vināyaka worship and leave Sāvitrī occupied with household work. They seat Gāyatrī and begin the rites and fire. Angry Sāvitrī declares failure and curses gods and sages to become insentient for seating the unauthorized wife. They request water and river forms instead, with a letter-equivalence phrase, and she assents. Śiva becomes Veṇyā, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇā and the others rivers bearing their names. The passage compares obstacles during Śiva’s destruction of Tripura when Gaṇeśa was neglected.

event.details: Brahmā and the goddesses acknowledge the neglected worship and plan devotion. The women go to the Rāma-established Vakratunda image in Karnāṭaka; his victory is recalled briefly.

evidence.paraphrase: Brahmā is distressed that his sacrifice caused the gods’ river forms and resolves to please Vighnahartā. Pulomajā, Girijā, Chāyā, Kamalā and other goddesses ask why the senior wife and Gaṇeśa were neglected and how to find relief. Brahmā reassures them and prescribes devotion, which he will also perform. They go to Karnāṭaka to a Mandāra-root image installed by Rāma as Vakratunda. The passage reports that its Lord’s boons made Rāma victorious over Rākṣasa leaders and Daśānana and brought him home with his wife. The goddesses begin severe tapas.

event.details: Varied austerities initially fail. Following a sky instruction, all offer śamī leaves and receive the four-armed, TWO-TUSK, mouse-mounted vision with Siddhi and Buddhi.

evidence.paraphrase: The goddesses use name and mantra recitation, lotus and hero postures, fasting, sweeping, circumambulation, bows, standing on one great toe, meditation and hymns. After a long time the Lord is not pleased. They offer flowers, dūrvā, incense, lamps, food, gold, Mandāra and śamī in different ways. A sky voice says he will not be pleased without śamī, so all worship with its leaves. Gajānana appears compassionately: four arms, crown, armlets, necklaces and earrings, long ears, cheeks, TWO TUSKS, Siddhi and Buddhi, mouse mount and yellow garments. Radiant like crores of suns, he receives their joyful prostration and hymn.

event.details: The goddess hymn requests original forms and constant remembrance. Gaṇeśa preserves Sāvitrī’s curse through river portions while restoring gods’ forms and offices. They apologize and worship.

evidence.paraphrase: At Kīrti’s request Gṛtsamada gives the goddesses’ hymn, praising the all-formed inner ruler, infinite power, refuge, many manifestations and weapons, world-protection and grants. They request the watery gods’ original forms and uninterrupted remembrance. Pleased, Gaṇeśa grants their wishes: Sāvitrī’s word cannot be made false, so gods recover original forms and offices while portions remain as rivers. He orders śamī worship, saying a leaf equals offering the world and gives the fruit of a hundred bhāras of gold. The gods actually regain their forms while river portions remain. They ask forgiveness for neglecting the elder wife and deity through delusion, rejoice and worship with leaves.

event.details: Gods install the stone Heramba temple at Supattana; Indra takes the earlier Mandāra image. Divine offices and household joys return. Brahmā performs twelve YEARS of tapas and repeats the sacrifice.

evidence.paraphrase: The Lord accepts and disappears. Gods install a stone image with four arms, trunk and elephant face, called Heramba, and a temple at Supattana for the world’s benefit. They promise all desires through devotional worship, remembrance and bowing. Indra takes the earlier Mandāra image to his city and worships it with his wife. Gods return to their offices, make Mandāra images and worship with śamī, enjoying their spouses and fulfilled desires. After twelve YEARS of tapas, Brahmā pleases Vighneśa and repeats the sacrifice. He worships a Mandāra image with śamī, gold leaves, dūrvā, Mandāra, ketaka and white dūrvā.

event.details: Gṛtsamada applies the plant account to the child’s revival and asks to leave. Kīrti bows and dismisses him; devotional hearing and morning remembrance fruits close the account, before another question in38.

evidence.paraphrase: Gṛtsamada tells Kīrti that hearing Mandāra and śamī’s glory removes sin, and her unknowing worship caused the child’s revival. He asks permission to go home. Hearing the account, she bows and dismisses her son’s reviver. The narrator promises no distress and fulfilled desires for hearing this story, and sinlessness and happiness through morning devotional remembrance of śamī, Mandāra and Gaṇeśa.
